description: Participants practise the work before and after an analysis, using requests from Ghadeer Water Company, a fictional water utility. They turn vague requests into decision questions with an estimand, a metric and a decision rule, interview a role-played manager, use domain knowledge of metering, billing and repair to see where the data mislead, and test whether data and deadline make the question answerable. They then review analyses by peers and by an assistant and write review notes ranked by consequence. Metric definition is DS-307; team review standards are DS-407.
audience: Practitioners. Data scientists and analysts who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: an analysis they framed, carried out and explained to a stakeholder.
prerequisites: DS-204 Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation
Has completed at least one analysis for a stakeholder
Reads a notebook in Python or R and reruns it

outcomes.text: Prepare a decision question with estimand, population, metric and decision rule from a vague request, given five requests from the utility's managers
outcomes.evidence: framing cards a peer can plan from without further questions

outcomes.text: Analyse a metric set for proxy failure and gaming, and propose guardrail metrics, given the utility's metric tree for water loss and customer service
outcomes.evidence: an annotated tree with two guardrails and the behaviour each prevents

outcomes.text: Use domain documents and an expert interview to map how the data behind a metric are produced, given a briefing pack on metering, billing cycles and leak repair, and a role-played engineer
outcomes.evidence: a process map marking three points where the data can mislead

outcomes.text: Design an analysis plan stating data, method, threats to validity and the result that would change the decision, given a framed question, a data inventory and a two-week deadline
outcomes.evidence: a two-page plan scored against a rubric

outcomes.text: Review an analysis for errors in question fit, data handling, method, inference and communication, given three seeded-flaw notebooks, one generated by an assistant
outcomes.evidence: review notes ranking the critical flaws by consequence, each with a fix

outcomes.text: Decide whether a request needs description, an experiment, a causal analysis, a predictive model or no analysis, given a role-played sponsor whose constraints change during the meeting
outcomes.evidence: a recommendation defended against the assessor's challenge
